claims.text: The starting feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder.
Conventionally bulk-manufactured AlCrFeNiSi exhibits significant cooling-induced compositional segregation.
Conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi exhibits high residual thermal stresses.
Conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi has a high incidence of process-induced defects.
Machine learning can be used to optimize an additive-manufacturing processing window by varying thermal boundary conditions and process parameters.
The proposed intervention adjusts cooling rates and laser scanning strategy using historical process data.
The relevant L-PBF regime involves rapid solidification and strong thermal gradients.
The optimized process will produce a more compositionally homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure with smaller compositional gradients.
The optimized process will refine the grain size.
The optimized microstructure will have a lower dislocation density.
The optimized microstructure will contain fewer thermal-stress concentration sites.
ML-optimized thermal management will reduce local thermal gradients during solidification.
Reducing local thermal gradients will diminish the driving force for compositional segregation.
Reducing local thermal gradients will diminish residual-stress accumulation.
Controlled cooling and remelting will improve grain refinement.
Optimization of thermal conditions and scanning strategy will decrease defect formation.
ML-optimized AlCrFeNiSi will have increased yield strength relative to conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi.
ML-optimized AlCrFeNiSi will have increased ductility relative to conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi.
The claimed validity is limited to laser-based additive manufacturing, particularly L-PBF, with room-temperature mechanical testing; applicability to casting and non-laser processes is unverified.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in segregation, residual stress, and defects or an improvement in yield strength and ductility versus a standard-L-PBF control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The comparator is not consistent: the hypothesis and baseline can include bulk conventional fabrication, the boundary says applicability to casting is unverified, and the decisive experiment compares optimized L-PBF only against standard L-PBF.
